blocks.text: Why terminology research is a major translation problem

Terminology research is a foundational task in professional translation. You must bridge the gap between source and target languages by identifying precise equivalents for specialized concepts. This is not just about finding a word. It is about finding the right word for a specific context. Technical terms often lack direct equivalents or have field-specific meanings that differ from general usage. For example, a term used in a medical manual might mean something entirely different in a legal document. Failing to identify these nuances leads to translation problems that can compromise the quality of your work.

Consistency is another major challenge. If you use varied translations for the same concept throughout a document, you confuse the reader. In specialized fields like engineering, this inconsistency can cause safety risks. You must resolve issues like polysemy, where one word has multiple meanings, and synonymy to ensure your target text is as precise as the source. Without a system, you are forced to perform manual lookups that break your concentration.
The financial and cognitive costs of inefficient research

Terminology management is a significant driver of project time and cost. When you spend too much time researching, your hourly rate effectively drops. A study on translating a 30-page, 211-item survey instrument found total costs reached 10,426 dollars. Personnel and overhead, including research and validation time, accounted for the vast majority of that expense. If you do not have an efficient way to manage terms, you end up paying for it with your own time.

Beyond money, there is the cognitive load. Translators juggle multiple tasks while working. Manual lookups are disruptive. In one study of survey translations, only 9 of 51 questions resulted in identical independent translations. Material differences often stemmed from the interpretation of technical and medical terminology. This shows that even professional translators struggle to achieve consistency without the right tools.
Fixes for terminology research without extra spending

items: Use Computer-Assisted Translation (CAT) tools. These are the industry standard for managing terminology. They allow you to create termbases that surface suggestions automatically.
Implement standardized workflows. Methods like TRAPD are used in high-stakes environments to ensure terminology is vetted by multiple experts.
Use centralized management. If you work in a team, use cloud-based terminology systems to share approved glossaries and prevent terminology bleed.
Organize your research tabs. Use tools like SupaSidebar on your Mac to keep project-specific reference tabs and dictionaries accessible without cluttering your browser.

blocks.text: If you translate for regulated industries like law, medicine, or finance, always follow your employer's rules regarding client data. Never paste sensitive information into public AI tools or unauthorized cloud services.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you research faster

Lazur is a voice assistant for your Mac that helps you manage your research workflow. When you are stuck on a term, you can hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about it. Lazur can look up definitions, synonyms, and usage examples directly from your screen. Because Lazur sees your screen, it understands the context of the document you are working on, making the research process much faster.
A simple routine for terminology management

items: Morning: Review your project glossary and add any new terms from the previous day.
Midday: Use your CAT tool for core translation, keeping your termbase open on a secondary display.
Afternoon: Dedicate 30 minutes to terminology research for the next day's segment.
Evening: Run a quick consistency check on your translated document to catch any lingering terminology issues.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you, points at things, or explains how to do something, but it does not click buttons or edit files for you.

faq.question: Is my data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots are not stored and are never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur with my CAT tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can use it to research terms while your CAT tool is open.
